In [[algebraic geometry]], a '''quasi-coherent sheaf''' on an [[algebraic stack]] <math>\mathfrak{X}</math> is a generalization of a [[quasi-coherent sheaf]] on a [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]]. The most concrete description is that it is a data that consists of, for each a scheme ''S'' in the base category and <math>\xi</math> in <math>\mathfrak{X}(S)</math>, a quasi-coherent sheaf <math>F_{\xi}</math> on ''S'' together with maps implementing the compatibility conditions among <math>F_{\xi}</math>'s.

For a [[Deligne–Mumford stack]], there is a simpler description in terms of a presentation <math>U \to \mathfrak{X}</math>: a quasi-coherent sheaf on <math>\mathfrak{X}</math> is one obtained by [[Descent (mathematics)|descending]] a quasi-coherent sheaf on ''U''.<ref>{{harvnb|Arbarello|Cornalba|Griffiths|2011|loc=Ch. XIII., § 2.}}</ref> A quasi-coherent sheaf on a Deligne–Mumford stack generalizes an [[orbibundle]] (in a sense).

[[Constructible sheaf|Constructible sheaves]] (e.g., as [[l-adic sheaf|ℓ-adic sheaves]]) can also be defined on an algebraic stack and they appear as coefficients of [[cohomology of a stack]].

== Definition ==
The following definition is {{harv|Arbarello|Cornalba|Griffiths|2011|loc=Ch. XIII., Definition 2.1.}}

Let <math>\mathfrak{X}</math> be a [[fibered category|category fibered]] in [[groupoid]]s over the category of schemes of finite type over a field with the structure functor ''p''. Then a quasi-coherent sheaf on <math>\mathfrak{X}</math> is the data consisting of:
# for each object <math>\xi</math>, a quasi-coherent sheaf <math>F_{\xi}</math> on the scheme <math>p(\xi)</math>,
# for each morphism <math>H: \xi \to \eta</math> in <math>\mathfrak{X}</math> and <math>h = p(H): p(\xi) \to p(\eta)</math> in the base category, an isomorphism
#:<math>\rho_H: h^*(F_{\eta}) \overset{\simeq}\to F_{\xi}</math>
:satisfying the cocycle condition: for each pair <math>H_1: \xi_1 \to \xi_2, H_2: \xi_2 \to \xi_3</math>,
::<math>h_1^* h_2^* F_{\xi_3} \overset{h_1^* (\rho_{H_2})} \to h_1^* F_{\xi_2} \overset{\rho_{H_1}}\to F_{\xi_1}</math> equals <math>h_1^* h_2^* F_{\xi_3} \overset{\sim}= (h_2 \circ h_1)^* F_{\xi_3} \overset{\rho_{H_2 \circ H_1}}\to F_{\xi_1}</math>.
(cf. [[equivariant sheaf]].)

== Examples ==
*The [[Hodge bundle]] on the [[moduli stack of algebraic curves]] of fixed genus.

== ℓ-adic formalism ==
{{expand section|date=April 2019}}

The [[ℓ-adic formalism]] (theory of ℓ-adic sheaves) extends to algebraic stacks.

== See also ==

* [[Hopf algebroid]] - encodes the data of quasi-coherent sheaves on a prestack presentable as a groupoid internal to affine schemes (or projective schemes using graded Hopf algebroids)
